description:
Create a new form. Provide exactly one of:
- `fields` (with `name`): use this when you already know the questions. It is instant and exact.
- `description`: a natural-language brief; niceform's AI designs the form (takes 10-60 seconds).

Set `publish: true` to make the form live right away, optionally with `close_at` (deadline) and `response_limit`. Without it the form is a draft: use get_preview_url to look at it, then publish_form.

niceform does not send the form to anyone. Once published, share the returned `publicUrl` with respondents yourself (email, chat, etc.). To check on results later, call summarize_responses for totals, or list_form_responses with `since` (the previous `latestSubmittedAt`) for new answers. Call close_form when collection is over.

Examples:
- fields: [{label: "Name", type: "text", required: true}, {label: "Attending?", type: "radio", options: ["Yes", "No"]}], name: "Party RSVP"
- description: "Create a customer feedback form for a restaurant with rating scales and comments"

close_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp with offset after which the form stops accepting responses. Requires publish: true.

description.description: Natural language brief for niceform to design the form (10-60 s). Mutually exclusive with fields.

fields.description: Exact questions, in order. Mutually exclusive with description; requires name.

options.description: Required for select, radio and checkboxes (unique values); not allowed for other types.

idempotency_key.description: A caller-generated unique key (preferably a UUID) for this intended form creation. Reuse the same key when retrying the same request.

one_response_per_device.description: Allow only one response per device.

response_limit.description: Maximum responses to accept. Requires publish: true.

style_preference.description: Optional style preference for the form appearance. Default uses organization branding.

name: create_form

publicUrl.description: Present when published; share this with respondents.
